question: What is the complete institutional verdict on DigitalOcean (NYSE: DOCN) as of November 13, 2026—for fresh capital, for our existing 78.07-share + LEAPS position, and for capital redeployment?

epigraph.quote: Separate the quality of the turnaround from the quality of the tape: admire the 40% ARR acceleration, respect the 50% gross-margin reality, and never hold an oversized Stage 4 equity.
epigraph.author: Executive Investment Committee

web_blocks.text: Executive Thesis: A Real AI Turnaround Trapped in a Stage 4, Capex-Heavy Wrapper

web_blocks.html: DigitalOcean (NYSE: DOCN) has delivered a sharp top-line turnaround under CEO Paddy Srinivasan [1][12]. Q3 2026 revenue rose 40% YoY to $321.2M (~$1.28B–$1.29B ARR), led by $376M in AI Customer ARR (+288% YoY) [1]. Ninety percent of AI revenue overlaps with Core Cloud, and ~60% of sales come from 4+ product users [1]. Yet GAAP gross margin fell ~980 bps to ~50.1% in Q3 2026 [1][2]. Heavy capex and financed equipment ($266.7M in FY25; $199.5M in 9M26) keep normalized ROIC near 7%–9% [2][3].

On November 13, 2026, DOCN closed at $86.32 (-53.96% from its $187.50 high; $10.19B mcap; $11.39B EV) [23][25]. It trades at 10.33x TTM EV/Sales and 9.41x FY26E sales [1][25]. Technically, the stock sits in Weinstein Stage 4 (-31.96% below its $126.87 30W SMA) inside a US Correction regime [23][29].

web_blocks.text: Key Execution Triggers & What Would Change Our Mind

web_blocks.html: Our REJECTED (TIER_0) rating would change only if two milestones are met. First, GAAP gross margins must hold at 50%–52% while all-in capex moderates, lifting ROIC above 10%–12% [1][2]. Second, DOCN must form a Stage 1 base above $67.44 and reclaim its 30-week SMA ($126.87) [23]. Until then, we execute EXIT_ON_BOUNCE on our 78.065338 shares ($98.00 / $112.90; $78.00 close stop).

Proceeds from exiting 78.065338 DOCN shares (~$6,738.60 at CMP, or ~$7,650–$8,200 on bounce fills) rotate systematically. We allocate 50% to Stage 2 Microsoft (MSFT) at $523.88 (BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO, support $507.61–$526.78, stop $452.41, target $660.00, 1.90:1 R:R). We hold 50% in Cash / T-Bills given the 6-distribution-day Correction [29]. Lower-multiple peer Akamai (AKAM) ($85.40, 4.16x EV/Sales) stays at 0% [26].

All figures are anchored to the November 13, 2026 close ($86.32) and Q3 2026 SEC filings [1][2][23]. Chapters 1–6 cover the price-blind business and financial forensics. Chapters 7–8 cover Reverse DCF valuation and Stage 4 technicals, and Chapter 9 details our action plan.

web_blocks.text: Why Business Quality and Tape Timing Diverge

web_blocks.html: Investors often struggle when a company's sales accelerate while its stock chart breaks down. DigitalOcean is a textbook case of that split in late 2026. On the product side, AI Customer ARR grew 288% YoY to $376M in Q3 2026 [1]. Total ARR hit ~$1.28B–$1.29B, up 40% YoY on a record $160M of net-new ARR [1]. Those numbers prove real customer demand, not hype. Yet on the financial side, GPU hardware and colocation leases cut GAAP gross margin to ~50.1% [1][2]. Adding $126.8M of financed equipment in FY2025 and $75.1M in 9M 2026 kept normalized ROIC near 7%–9% [2][3]. Until margins stabilize and the chart builds a Stage 1 base above $67.44, discipline beats hope [23].

Our portfolio plan reflects both facts cleanly. We reject new equity capital at Tier 0 because the trend and cash-flow gates fail. At the same time, we do not panic-sell our 78.065338 shares at the lows. Instead, we use the 4-hour bounce to sell 39.0 shares at $98.00 and 39.065338 shares at $112.90. A hard daily-close stop at $78.00 protects the downside ahead of the $80.00 LEAPS floor. Every freed dollar then shifts 50% into Stage 2 MSFT and 50% into Cash.

This dual verdict separates business admiration from capital discipline. DigitalOcean's 288% AI ARR growth and 90% Core Cloud overlap are genuine operational wins [1]. Even so, 50.1% gross margins, heavy equipment financing, and a Stage 4 downtrend argue against fresh equity [1][2][23]. By staging exits on our 78.065338 shares at $98.00 and $112.90, we protect against further drawdowns. Rotating half into Stage 2 MSFT and half into Cash keeps the portfolio aligned with market reality.

Every number in this report traces back to SEC filings and live November 13, 2026 market quotes [1][2][23]. We keep business quality and price action strictly separate before combining them into one clear portfolio decision. That discipline prevents strong top-line growth from masking a Stage 4 chart or heavy GPU capital intensity.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to the institutional monograph on DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc., ticker DOCN on the New York Stock Exchange, as of the November 13, 2026 market close. At $86.32 per share—a $10.19 billion market capitalization and $11.39 billion enterprise value—DigitalOcean sits at the intersection of two competing narratives. On one side stands a remarkably executed operational turnaround under CEO Paddy Srinivasan, who has re-accelerated revenue growth to 40% year-over-year, scaled AI Customer ARR by 288% to $376 million, and proved that 90% of AI customers also adopt Core Cloud workflows. On the other side stands the cold arithmetic of infrastructure economics: a 980-basis-point GAAP gross margin compression down to 50.1%, heavy reliance on cash capex and equipment financing, a normalized ROIC hovering near 7% to 9%, and a stock price locked in a Weinstein Stage 4 downtrend nearly 32% below its 30-week moving average.

Our research separates business quality from tape timing before synthesizing both into a disciplined portfolio decision. In Chapters 1 through 6, we evaluate DigitalOcean blind to its share price and conclude that the company earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality verdict with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. In Chapters 7 through 9, we layer on valuation, reverse DCF expectations, multi-timeframe technicals, and our portfolio ledger.

In sum, DigitalOcean is a business to admire for its 2026 operational turnaround and AI customer pull-through, but a stock to respect for its Stage 4 technical breakdown and heavy GPU capital intensity. We reject fresh equity capital at Tier 0, exit our common shares into strength or below $78.00, and upgrade portfolio quality toward Microsoft and Cash.

book_subsections.title: The Bottom Line for New Capital and Held Positions
paragraphs: For fresh capital, our verdict is REJECTED at Conviction Tier 0, gated by both TREND and CASH_FLOW. With a 12-month probability-weighted expected value of $98.60 (+14.2%) against a $56.00 bear case (-35.1%), the reward-to-risk profile does not justify catching a Stage 4 falling knife in a Correction market.

For our existing portfolio—which holds 78.065338 common shares worth $6,738.60 alongside four June 2027 $150 Call LEAPS worth $3,720.00, representing an outsized 11.8% combined weight of our $88,684.68 net worth—our action is EXIT_ON_BOUNCE. We use the developing 4-hour momentum turn to sell 39.0 shares at $98.00 and 39.065338 shares at $112.90, with a hard stop-loss on a close below $78.00, redeploying 50% into Stage 2 Microsoft (MSFT) and 50% into Cash.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Monograph
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 are written strictly price-blind: they trace DigitalOcean's evolution from Techstars Boulder to a $1.28 billion ARR AI cloud platform, dissect its Core Cloud versus GPU unit economics, benchmark it against hyperscalers and neoclouds, audit management's KPIs, and reconstruct its cash-flow and convertible-debt forensics. Chapters 7 through 9 then remove the blindfold—testing what $86.32 prices in via Reverse DCF, mapping the Stage 4 weekly breakdown and 4H bounce mechanics, and delivering our binding New Capital Rejection, Exit-on-Bounce execution alerts, and MSFT/Cash redeployment plan.
